channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Fio do Professor Felipe Nunes: análise da pesquisa Quaest para presidente de 14 de agosto
item.description: The Quaest poll from August 14 shows Lula leading Flávio in the first round with 38% to 31%, though his advantage has narrowed compared to previous surveys. In a potential runoff, the two are technically tied within the margin of error at 43% to 40%, signaling a still-polarized and undecided race. Lula leads among Northeasterners, low-income voters, Catholics, and the less educated, while Flávio performs better among evangelicals, wealthier voters, Southerners, and those with higher education.

item.title: Agregador: Campanha começa com distância de 4 pontos entre Lula e Flávio
item.description: The presidential campaign for the runoff begins on Sunday (16) with Lula (PT) leading Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) by four percentage points, according to UOL's poll aggregator. The advantage suggests an initially favorable scenario for the incumbent president, though the margin is considered relatively narrow for a runoff. The aggregator combines multiple polls to provide a weighted average of voting intentions.

item.title: Quaest mostra Lula com 43% e Flávio Bolsonaro com 40% em empate técnico no 2º turno
item.description: A Quaest poll released on Friday, August 14, shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a technical tie for a potential second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, with Lula at 43% and Bolsonaro at 40% in voter intention. The results indicate a highly competitive race, within the margin of error, suggesting neither candidate holds a clear advantage.

item.title: Lula tem 43% e Flávio, 40%, em eventual segundo turno, aponta pesquisa Quaest
item.description: In a hypothetical runoff for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leads with 43% of voting intentions, while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) trails with 40%, according to a Quaest poll. The 3-point difference falls within the margin of error, indicating a technical tie. The result reflects ongoing polarization between Lula’s base and Bolsonaro’s political movement.

item.title: Quaest: Lula e Flávio voltam a ficar empatados no 2º turno
item.description: The Quaest poll released today shows President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) technically tied in the second round of the 2026 presidential election, with 43% and 40% of voting intentions, respectively. The statistical margin of error places both candidates within a technical tie range, indicating an extremely close race.

item.title: Violência é maior preocupação entre eleitores, mostra Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll released on March 14 shows violence as the top concern among Brazilian voters, cited by 33% of respondents, followed by economy (15%), health (14%) and corruption (14%). The survey was commissioned by Globo in partnership with O Globo and is part of a series of 130 polls to be published until October 3, the eve of the first round of the 2026 elections, covering presidential, senatorial and gubernatorial races across all states and the Federal District.

item.title: Renan Santos denuncia ameaça de morte antes de ato de campanha
item.description: Renan Santos, national president of Missão and pre-candidate for President of Brazil, reported an anonymous death threat published on the Leftypol forum, which was later deleted. The threat, stating 'I WILL KILL RENAN SANTOS!', was forwarded to the party via a screenshot. The incident occurred ahead of a campaign event.

item.title: Quaest indica Lula à frente de Flávio em segundo turno
item.description: Genial/Quaest poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading with 43% of voting intentions in a potential runoff against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who has 40%. Another 13% of voters are undecided, blank, or null. The survey tested four runoff scenarios, with Lula also ahead of Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema.

item.title: Quaest: desaprovação volta a passar numericamente a aprovação do governo Lula
item.description: The Quaest poll shows that disapproval of President Lula's government has again surpassed approval, with 48% disapproving and 46% approving, within the poll's two-point margin of error. Key drivers of declining support include Federal Police investigations into his son Fábio Luis over alleged influence-peddling in health, favors at Dataprev, and illicit deals, alongside Lula's political outreach to congressional leaders to advance his agenda before the first round.

item.title: Governo Lula é aprovado por 46% e desaprovado por 48%, diz Quaest
item.description: President Lula's government has a 46% approval rate and 48% disapproval, with 36% rating his administration as positive, 25% as regular, and 37% as negative, according to a Quaest poll from August 2026. In a hypothetical runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula leads with 43% voting intention versus 40% for his opponent, maintaining a slight edge from the previous survey. The poll surveyed 2,004 Brazilian voters between August 10–13, with a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Quaest presidencial: Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula lideram em rejeição na disputa presidencial; veja índices
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro lead in rejection in the Quaest poll, with 52% and 54% respectively, while maintaining high vote potential (45% and 41%). Other candidates like Caiado and Zema have lower vote potential and high voter unfamiliarity. The survey was conducted after the STF authorized an investigation into Fábio Luís Lula da Silva on suspicion of influence peddling.

item.title: Quaest presidencial: Lula lidera cenários de 2º turno; petista tem 43% contra 40% de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Lula leads with 43% against Flávio Bolsonaro's 40% in a potential second-round scenario, with the difference within the margin of error, indicating a technical tie. The Quaest poll, conducted between Monday and Thursday with 2,004 voters, shows Flávio's recovery following the revelation of his conversations with Daniel Vorcaro. Other scenarios show Lula leading Caiado (44% to 37%), Renan Santos (44% to 36%), and Romeu Zema (45% to 34%).

item.title: Flávio ficou à frente de Lula em enquete, e não pesquisa eleitoral
item.description: Social media posts falsely claim that an electoral poll showed Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 68.4% voting intention against 9.5% for President Lula (PT). In reality, the figure comes from an informal, non-scientific online poll with no statistical validity or recognized methodology. The misinformation attempts to create a misleading narrative about Bolsonaro’s electoral standing compared to the current president.

item.title: Quaest presidencial: Lula tem 38% contra 31% de Flávio no 1º turno; Caiado, Renan e Zema seguem em 3º
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of the 2026 presidential election with 38% to 31%, respectively. Caiado and Renan are tied at 4%, while Zema has 2%. In a potential runoff, Lula would have 43% and Flávio 40%. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters from Monday to Thursday, with a margin of error of two percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Quaest: 46% aprovam e 48% desaprovam governo Lula
item.description: The Quaest poll released on August 14, 2026 shows President Lula's approval at 46% and disapproval at 48%, with 6% undecided. Government approval is nearly tied: 36% positive, 37% negative, and 25% regular. A majority (53%) believe Brazil is heading in the wrong direction, and 49% say the economy has worsened over the past year, though 42% expect improvement in the next 12 months.

item.title: Quaest, 2º turno: Lula, 43%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 40%
item.description: A Quaest poll released on August 14 shows Lula (PT) at 43% and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 40% in a potential second-round scenario, with a two-point margin of error. The survey interviewed 2,004 people between August 10 and 13, was commissioned by Globo and O Globo, and carries registration BR-06773/2026. Additional second-round matchups involving Lula against Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, and Romeu Zema were tested, but only the Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro figures were emphasized in the provided content.

item.title: Quaest, 1º turno: Lula, 38%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 31%; Renan Santos, 4%; Caiado, 4%; e Zema, 2%
item.description: The Quaest poll released on Friday shows Lula leading the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election with 38% voting intention, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 31%. Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema each received 4%, 4%, and 2%, respectively. The survey interviewed 2,004 people between August 10 and 13, with a margin of error of ±2 percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Matou o sigilo da fonte e foi ao Maranhão
item.description: Flavio Dino, former governor of Maranhão and STF minister, seeks to identify an informant of journalist Luís Pablo among his political adversaries, using secret inquiries to persecute critics under the guise of combating illegality. The action involves mobilizing the Supreme Federal Court against the current governor, Dino’s former ally, in a political-judicial conflict aimed at criminalizing investigative journalism by treating source shielding as a cover for illegal acts, despite no evidence against the journalist.

item.title: Leia a íntegra do plano de governo de Ronaldo Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD presidential candidate, unveiled a 26-area government plan emphasizing the end of re-election for executive offices, adoption of a mixed-district electoral system, a "Truth Budget" to curb spending and boost private investment to 25% of GDP, and hardline security measures including labeling PCC and Comando Vermelho as domestic terrorism and reducing the age of criminal responsibility to 16 for serious crimes.

item.title: Dani Lima: Centrão indica se afastar de Flávio para viabilizar nomes no NE
item.description: The centrão is signaling a distancing from Flávio Bolsonaro to preserve local alliances and enable candidacies, particularly in the Northeast, according to Daniela Lima on UOL News. The move aims to balance regional political forces ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Ibovespa encerra em queda pelo 9° pregão consecutivo; entenda
item.description: The Ibovespa closed lower for the ninth consecutive trading session, reaching 166,900 points, driven by foreign capital outflows, concerns over Brazil's gross debt and fiscal outlook, and electoral uncertainties. Major banks such as Itaú, Banco do Brasil, and Santander rose, while Bradesco declined. The dollar ended higher at R$ 5.21.

item.title: O otimismo de Motta sobre postura de Lula em relação à disputa eleitoral da Paraíba
item.description: Allies of Hugo Motta downplay Lula's silence regarding concrete support for Nabor Wanderley, father of the Chamber president and Senate candidate in Paraíba, despite Motta formalizing his support for Lula's re-election and receiving a thank-you call. While Lula has publicly backed Senator Veneziano Vital do Rêgo, the call and hint of a meeting after Motta's alignment are interpreted as a gesture of unity among allies.

item.title: Áudio: Desigualdade será tema de debate na Comissão de Assuntos Sociais do Senado
item.description: The Senate's Commission on Social Affairs will hold a debate on inequality in Brazil, at the request of Senator Paulo Paim (PT-RS), rapporteur of the bill establishing August as National Month to Combat Social Inequality. Minister Guilherme Boulos, former deputy and author of the bill, will be one of the guests at the public hearing, date yet to be set.

item.title: “Tinha de falar mal do Real” em 1994 por razões eleitorais, diz Lula
item.description: In an interview with the podcast Inteligência Ltda. on July 30, 2026, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) admitted he criticized the Real Plan in 1994 for electoral reasons, needing to differentiate himself from Fernando Henrique Cardoso (PSDB), who was winning the presidential race due to the plan’s success. Lula stated that, as the candidate of the PT and PC do B, he had to oppose the Real to maintain a distinct political stance, even while acknowledging it as an 'extraordinary success' that stabilized inflation.

item.title: Clica e Confirma destaca início da campanha eleitoral nas ruas e na internet neste domingo (16)
item.description: The program Clica e Confirma highlighted the start of electoral campaigning on the streets and online for Brazil’s 2026 General Elections, which became permitted this Sunday (16), in accordance with TSE Resolution No. 23.760/2026. The episode featured Eilzon Almeida, a judicial analyst from the TSE, who explained electoral legislation rules, campaign limits, and channels for reporting violations to the Electoral Justice.

item.title: TSE discutirá em plenário decisão de Mendonça que mandou governo informar gastos com publicidade
item.description: The TSE will discuss in plenary the decision by Minister André Mendonça requiring the Lula government to disclose public advertising spending from 2023 to 2026, after a highlight request voided the virtual vote. The PL-led action alleges excessive institutional advertising spending in the first half of 2026, potentially violating Brazil's Election Law (Art. 73, VII, Law 9.504/1997). Court President Kassio Nunes Marques will set the date for the in-person session.

item.title: Flávio e Marinho rebatem Kassab: “Minha disputa é resgatar o Brasil”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and his campaign coordinator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) rebutted statements by Gilberto Kassab (PSD), who doubted Flávio Bolsonaro’s electoral chances. They asserted that their campaign aims to 'rescue Brazil', emphasizing opposition to what they describe as a detrimental political project. The response was delivered in a press conference on Friday, the 14th, reinforcing confidence in their campaign.

item.title: Dólar sobe e Bolsa tem 9ª queda seguida com fuga de estrangeiros
item.description: The dollar rose 0.52% against the real, reaching R$5.22, while the Ibovespa marked its ninth consecutive decline, closing down 0.13% at 166,8 thousand points after hitting a low of 164,8 thousand points during the session. The pressure stems from foreign capital outflows, driven by JPMorgan’s downgrade of Brazil’s investment outlook due to expected electoral volatility and fiscal uncertainty. Analysts say investors are shifting funds to mature markets like the U.S., particularly in tech and AI, erasing much of the Ibovespa’s 2026 gains.

item.title: Suplente de Derrite foi demitido por Bolsonaro por usar avião da FAB
item.description: Vicente Santini, selected as the alternate candidate for Guilherme Derrite’s Senate ticket in São Paulo, was fired by Jair Bolsonaro in 2021 for using a Brazilian Air Force (FAB) plane to travel to India, which Bolsonaro labeled 'immoral' despite legal justification from the FAB and Civil House. After his dismissal, Santini was reassigned to another role in the Civil House and now serves as a coordinator for Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro sinaliza em programa de governo que dívida pode ser sua âncora fiscal
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's government program signals a potential shift in Brazil's fiscal anchor, suggesting public debt could replace the spending ceiling as the fiscal reference point, though without specifying concrete measures. The document emphasizes discretionary spending control, administrative reform, ending supersalaries, and anti-fraud measures in Social Security, while leaving undefined the treatment of mandatory spending and a replacement for the spending cap. The campaign avoids deep commitments, citing the need for legal security and ongoing policy evaluation to achieve fiscal balance.

item.title: Advogado de Carla Zambelli quer ação para investigar Lulinha
item.description: Fabio Pagnozzi, lawyer for ex-deputy Carla Zambelli, announced he will request the Spanish Public Prosecutor's Office to investigate Synapta SL, the company of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), eldest son of President Lula. Pagnozzi claims he verified the company's Madrid address is a fiscal address with no real activity, suspecting a shell company and questioning who funds Lulinha in Spain.

item.title: Crusoé: Divirta-se com o plano de governo de Augusto Cury
item.description: Augusto Cury, candidate for the Avante party and known as the world's most-read psychiatrist, filed his government plan with the TSE. His candidacy is framed as an act of voluntarism aimed at healing others' suffering, emphasizing his international publishing reach across more than 90 countries. The piece highlights his emotional and symbolic appeal rather than concrete public policy proposals.

item.title: 'Liberdade de imprensa não está em questão no Brasil', diz Cármen Lúcia
item.description: STF Minister Carmen Lucia stated that press freedom is not in question in Brazil, emphasizing the constitutional guarantee of source confidentiality. She declined to comment on the specific case involving a police operation against a source linked to reports critical of Minister Flávio Dino, but said she will vote when the matter reaches the Supreme Court plenary. Her remarks were made during a BBC World Service and BBC News Brasil event on combating disinformation.

item.title: “Quem foi a liderança nacional mais recente? Eu e Bolsonaro”, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula stated that he and former President Jair Bolsonaro are the only national leaders in the current political landscape, noting that Bolsonaro has support in every Brazilian state. The comment was made during an interview on the podcast 'Não Inviabilize'.

item.title: Grêmio lança 3º uniforme em homenagem aos 30 anos da tríplice coroa
item.description: Grêmio unveiled its third kit in honor of the 30th anniversary of the 1996 treble, which included the Gaúcho, Brasileirão, and Recopa Sul-Americana titles. The jersey will debut in the match against Chapecoense on August 30, valid for the 25th round of the Brazilian Championship. The launch event featured players from the men's, women's, and under-20 squads, as well as Dinho, who participated in the 1996 triumphs.

item.title: Lula questionou Lulinha sobre natureza da relação com lobista investigada no esquema do INSS, afirmam aliados
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reportedly questioned his son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), about the nature of his friendship with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation in the INSS influence-peddling scheme. According to allies, Lula raised the concern in a phone call prior to former chief of staff Marco Aurélio Ribeiro Santana being targeted, saying the relationship seemed 'strange' given his presidential status. Lulinha reportedly explained that Luchsinger has been a close friend of his wife for nearly ten years. Lula stated he had asked his son’s lawyers not to seek dismissal of the ongoing investigations.

item.title: Salário mínimo: governo projeta piso de R$ 1.741 em 2027
item.description: The Lula government has updated its projection for Brazil's 2027 minimum wage to R$1,741, up R$24 from the April estimate of R$1,717, reflecting revised inflation forecasts. This represents a 7.4% increase over the current R$1,621 minimum wage and will be included in the 2026 budget bill to be submitted to Congress on July 31. The adjustment will affect pensions, social benefits, unemployment insurance, and MEI contributions, as nearly 45% of RGPS benefits are tied to the minimum wage.

item.title: Patrus troca 1º debate em Minas por lançamento da campanha de Lula
item.description: Patrus Ananias (PT) announced he will not attend the first gubernatorial debate in Minas Gerais, scheduled for this Sunday (August 16) on Band Minas, because he will be in São Bernardo do Campo attending the launch of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s (PT) re-election campaign. He stated that the commitment with Lula was pre-arranged and he cannot return to Belo Horizonte in time for the debate, though he confirmed his presence in upcoming debates with other broadcasters.

item.title: Michelle estuda pedido ao STF para acompanhar estreia de Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro is considering requesting authorization from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to allow a trusted person to accompany former President Jair Bolsonaro during the first official campaign event of her son, Flávio Bolsonaro, for the presidency, scheduled for this Sunday in Copacabana. Her participation in the event depends on resolving the care situation for the former president, who is under judicial restrictions.

item.title: Com erro em registro, candidato do Agir declara ter R$ 1,5 quatrilhão
item.description: Tiago Társis, the Agir party's Senate candidate for the Federal District, had a typo in his asset declaration filed with the TSE, showing R$1.5 quadrillion instead of the correct R$15,000. He explained the error came from a website patent declaration and said the party will correct it. Társis stated he had tried to declare the accurate amount before the election to do the right thing.

item.title: Rogério Marinho reage a Kassab e diz que PSD atua para eleger Lula
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) criticized PSD national president Gilberto Kassab after Kassab stated that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has no chance of winning the 2026 presidential election. Marinho accused the PSD of acting as an 'auxiliary line' for Lula's government, citing three PSD ministers in the federal cabinet and claiming Ronaldo Caiado's candidacy is not genuine. He argued the political system has united against Flávio Bolsonaro due to feeling threatened.

item.title: Jovem deixa rastros e assume que tentou filiar Lula ao Missão
item.description: A 16-year-old admitted attempting to register President Lula with the far-right Missão party to expose flaws in the TSE’s voter registration system, following a similar incident involving Flávio Bolsonaro. He provided his personal phone number, email containing his name and other identifiers, and used Lula’s official data, arguing the system is too vulnerable to impersonation. Missão canceled the registration before it was processed and filed a judicial complaint for ideological fraud.

item.title: Fernando Holiday diz que Missão 'cometeu crime' em filiação fraudulenta de Flávio Bolsonaro: 'Moleques irresponsáveis e burros'
item.description: Former councilman Fernando Holiday accused the Missão party of committing a crime by facilitating a fraudulent affiliation that blocked Flávio Bolsonaro from registering his presidential candidacy under the PL. He claims the party had knowledge of the issue since at least August 2, contradicting its claim of being caught off guard, and argues that its reaction is inconsistent with its own timeline.

item.title: Zema inicia campanha presidencial com missa em Montes Claros
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential candidate for the Novo party, launched his official campaign in Montes Claros, Minas Gerais, with a mass at the Nossa Senhora da Conceição e São José parish. The choice of this city in northern Minas Gerais reflects an effort to expand his base beyond the Southeast, emphasizing his image as a technical and moderate manager. The event marked the symbolic start of his 2026 electoral journey.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: A seletividade processual do Direito Xandônico
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program analyzed the procedural selectivity of Minister Alexandre de Moraes in a case involving a Maranhão journalist who disclosed sensitive information about Minister Flávio Dino. It also discussed the start of the 2026 electoral campaign, highlighting the registration of Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy.

item.title: Parlamentares defendem rigor penal no plano de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Allied lawmakers of Flávio Bolsonaro advocate for stricter penal legislation as a priority in their public security plan, including prison system expansion and measures against criminal organizations. The proposal aligns with Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) government plan, which centers on hardline penal policies as a core campaign pillar.

item.title: Integrantes do governo não acreditam que reciprocidade contra os EUA seja aplicada antes da eleição
item.description: Lula’s government officials believe effective reciprocity against U.S. tariffs will not be applied before the October elections, as the process takes 60–90 days. They prefer alternatives like suspending U.S. intellectual property royalties over direct taxation to avoid harming Brazil’s economy. They also expect the U.S. to only resume negotiations after the election, with differing expectations depending on whether Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro wins.

item.title: Quem são os candidatos que mais arrecadaram em vaquinhas para as eleições de 2026? Veja ranking
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) leads the 2026 electoral crowdfunding ranking with R$1.23 million raised, followed by Marcel van Hattem (Novo) and Jones Manoel (PSOL). The three candidates together have raised approximately R$2.5 million through TSE-homologated crowdfunding platforms, indicating growing digital supporter engagement.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral começa neste domingo; conheça as regras
item.description: Electoral campaigning for the 2026 elections officially begins this Sunday (16), allowing candidates to directly solicit votes, hold rallies, and conduct live internet broadcasts. Free radio and TV advertising starts on August 28, with 70 minutes daily allocated for 30- and 60-second spots. The TSE has established strict rules to ensure fairness and prevent abuses, banning deepfakes, audio/video manipulation, and requiring accountability for false, hateful, or antidemocratic content, while regulating AI use and social media in campaigns.

item.title: Alfredo Gaspar, vice de Flávio, declara R$ 565 mil de patrimônio
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar, running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the 2026 presidential ticket, declared R$ 564,666.16 in assets to the TSE in 2026, reflecting a real growth of 63.49% compared to his 2022 declaration, adjusted for inflation. His largest assets include a 2024 Jeep Compass (R$ 158,170.42), a house in Marechal Deodoro/AL (R$ 95,900.00), and a stake in a fuel station (R$ 27,345.31).
